newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HKMA to tender HK$10 bln more 28-day EF bills.
newsitem.headline: HKMA to tender HK$10 bln more 28-day EF bills.

text.p: Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said on Friday it will tender another issue of 28-day Exchange Fund bills on December 5 of up to HK$10 billion to meet strong demand.
Hong Kong's defacto central bank announced earlier this month that it would tender two special issues of 28-day EF bills of HK$5.0 billion each on November 26 and December 3.

"Despite the recent increase in the supply of short-term Exchange Fund bills, there remains very strong demand from banks for additional supply of bills in preparation for the implementation of the RTGS system," said a HKMA spokesman.

Under the Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system, which will start on December 9, banks can make use of Exchange Fund bills and notes to obtain interest free intraday liquidity by carrying out intraday repuchase transactions with the HKMA.

This fuelled strong demand on short-dated government paper and resulted in the continued widening of the spreads between the yields of Exchange Fund bills and the Hong Kong interbank rate (HIBOR), dealers said.
The HKMA said that after the tender of the first issue of 28-day bills on November 26, the spread continued to widen to 76 basis points on Friday from 59 basis points.
The spread of three-month bill yields to HIBOR also grew to 91 basis points from 74 basis points, it added.

The interbank market will have additional supply of short-term bills amounting to HK$20 billion in the initial weeks of the RTGS implementation, which should ensure adequate intraday liquidity for banks to manage their payment flows effectively under the system, the HKMA said.
